# A complete weighted polynomial estimate for the double characteristic operator

Research date: 16 October 2026. Status: internally derived, unreviewed. Historical priority and external verification are UNKNOWN. The supplied cubic theorem is inherited; the argument below extends its degree and defect exponent and proves necessity by exact compatible fields. It does not prove the sharp conformal quasiconvexity inequality.

## Statement

Use normalized averages and norms on the square two-dimensional torus. Put

\[
D\phi=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},\qquad
q=\sigma a+d,\qquad T_\sigma\phi=(q,c),\qquad \sigma>0.
\]

Let \(P\) be homogeneous of degree \(m\ge2\), and set

\[
\widetilde P(a,b,c,q)=P(a,b,c,q-\sigma a).
\]

Give these variables weights

\[
\operatorname{wt}(b)=0,\quad \operatorname{wt}(a)=1,
\quad \operatorname{wt}(c)=\operatorname{wt}(q)=2.
\]

Fix \(0<\alpha\le m\) and \(1<p,s<\infty\) satisfying

\[
\frac\alpha p+\frac{m-\alpha}{s}=1. \tag{A}
\]

Then the absolute estimate

\[
\|P(D\phi)\|_1\le K\|T_\sigma\phi\|_p^\alpha
                         \|D\phi\|_s^{m-\alpha} \tag{B}
\]

holds for all smooth periodic maps, with some finite \(K\), if and only if every nonzero monomial of \(\widetilde P\) has weight at least \(2\alpha\).

For \(m\ge3\), exactly the same criterion characterizes the signed estimate

\[
|\langle P(D\phi)\rangle|\le K\|T_\sigma\phi\|_p^\alpha
                         \|D\phi\|_s^{m-\alpha}. \tag{C}
\]

For \(m=2\), the signed criterion is instead that there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) for which every monomial of

\[
\widetilde P-\lambda(aq-\sigma a^2-bc)
\]

has weight at least \(2\alpha\). The subtracted expression is the true gradient determinant. Its average is zero. It must not be replaced by only its lowest weighted part \(-\sigma a^2-bc\).

The assertion passes by convolution to maps for which \(D\phi\in L^s\) and \(T_\sigma\phi\in L^p\). If \(p>s\), this second assumption is additional. The same criterion holds for smooth compactly supported maps, or the corresponding zero-boundary classes, on any nonempty bounded planar domain. Sufficiency follows by zero extension into a surrounding square; necessity also needs the localization argument below. Constants are unchanged by isotropic rescaling. No endpoint \(p=1,\infty\) or \(s=1,\infty\) is asserted.

Write \(E=\|T_\sigma\phi\|

16 October 2026. This version supersedes `EXTENSIONS_v1.md`, which is preserved internally. Two audit qualifications are incorporated: repeated same-source cosine modes are grouped before amplitudes are selected; periodic transfer under an arbitrary real coordinate change is proved by compact-support localization rather than asserted to be immediate. This remains internally derived and unreviewed externally. Historical priority is UNKNOWN.

## A. Finite bounded-frequency signed witnesses

Let \(R(a,b,c,q)\) be homogeneous of degree \(m\ge2\), and suppose its average under
\((a,b,c,q)=(\psi_{xy},\psi_{yy},-\sigma\psi_{xx},k)\) is not identically zero for periodic \(\psi\) and mean-zero \(k\). This holds for every nonzero \(R\) when \(m\ge3\); at degree two the excluded null span is \(-\sigma a^2-bc\).

Then there is a nonzero signed witness using a combined total of at most \(m\) distinct same-source cosine modes, with every cosine amplitude an integer between one and \(m+1\), and every frequency coordinate of absolute value at most \(5(m-1)\). A mode of \(\psi\) and a mode of \(k\) are distinct sources even when their cosine frequencies coincide. Rational \(\sigma>0\) and rational input coefficients make the finite search exactly rational.

\[
H(\nu)=(-\nu_x\nu_y,-\nu_y^2,\sigma\nu_x^2,0),
\qquad Q=(0,0,0,1).
\]

\[
B(\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_{m-1})
=m!\mathcal R(V_1,\ldots,V_m)\ne0,
\qquad \nu_m=-\sum_{i<m}\nu_i.
\]

For a fixed type assignment, \(B\) is a polynomial of degree at most four in each independent frequency coordinate: a coordinate appears in its own slot and the final slot, with degree at most two in each. Thus a nonzero \(B\) is detected on

\[
\nu_i\in\{1,2,3,4,5\}^2\quad(1\le i<m). \tag{1}

# Polynomial compensation across a double characteristic

16 October 2026. Repository reference supplied by the parent task: `astra-positive-memory-20261016`, commit `f80a8f15137575133ad2c9af975513b32e8fa93e`. No Git changes or external writes were made. This folder contains an internally derived theorem candidate and exact finite checks. External mathematical verification and historical priority remain **UNKNOWN**.

The strongest result is a complete polynomial/exponent classification for the degenerate conformal operator, together with a finite compiler for compatible failure sequences. A separate sharp quadratic inequality has both its optimal constant and optimal defect exponent. These results extend the supplied cubic selection rule. They do not settle the fixed-coefficient sharp conformal quasiconvexity inequality.

## Complete classification

Let \(D\phi=(a,b;c,d)\), \(q=\sigma a+d\), \(T_\sigma\phi=(q,c)\), with \(\sigma>0\). Express a homogeneous degree-\(m\) polynomial in \((a,b,c,q)\), and give these variables weights

\[
\operatorname{wt}(b)=0,\quad\operatorname{wt}(a)=1,
\quad\operatorname{wt}(c)=\operatorname{wt}(q)=2.
\]

For \(m\ge3\), \(0<\alpha\le m\), and finite \(1<p,s<\infty\) satisfying
\(\alpha/p+(m-\alpha)/s=1\), the following are equivalent:

1. \(|\langle P(D\phi)\rangle|\le K\|T_\sigma\phi\|_p^\alpha\|D\phi\|_s^{m-\alpha}\) for all periodic compatible maps.
2. The same estimate holds for \(\|P(D\phi)\|_1\).
3. Every monomial of \(P(a,b,c,q-\sigma a)\) has weight at least \(2\alpha\).

Degree two has one exact signed exception: subtract any multiple of the **true** determinant \(aq-\sigma a^2-bc\) before testing the low weights. The absolute criterion has no such exception. Degree one is excluded because every periodic linear gradient integral vanishes.

The statement includes periodic Sobolev maps with \(D\phi\in L^s\), \(T_\sigma\phi\in L^p\), and zero-boundary maps on nonempty bounded domains. Zero-boundary necessity uses periodic tiling, a large smooth cutoff, and isotropic rescaling. No endpoint estimate is asserted.

The analytic ingredient is the supplied mixed-derivative/Hodge estimate \(\|a\|_t^2\lesssim\|T_\sigma\phi\|_p\|D\phi\|_s\), with \(2/t=1/p+1/s\).
